name: 19334-sharedprefix-1.8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), on a 44-vCPU host.
architecture: Dense decoder (Qwen2ForCausalLM), 24 layers, 16 query heads, 16 KV heads (MHA), head_dim 128, hidden 2048, vocab 151936, 32768-token window, bf16, 1.84B params.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams = 100, bounded at 1000 requests / 900 s safety, warmup the first 10% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, one prefix bucket (bucket_weight 100, prefix_count 1, prefix_tokens 10000); prompt exactly 32 tokens and output exactly 1, so every request is 10000 shared + 32 unique = 10032 prompt tokens. `request_format: plain` in scenario.json sends one raw string with no chat template (the /v1/completions shape); the prefix text is faker prose.
purpose: A document-grounded lookup service on a small model, answering 100 concurrent one-word queries against a shared 10,000-token reference text on one GPU.
launch:
# vLLM at commit edd270bc781e5a3d250827ac7039d71b8562bb04.
# Interpreter and hardware: configs/env.yaml (per-machine, not portable).

model: Qwen/Qwen1.5-1.8B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
enforce-eager: true
trust-remote-code: true
dtype: bfloat16

# Load-bearing rather than decorative: the workload is one 10000-token prefix shared by
# every request, so with caching off this is a different experiment.
enable-prefix-caching: true

# Pinned because constructing the engine in process does not reach this engine's
# usage-context default table; without these two, both fall through to SchedulerConfig's
# own defaults (max_num_seqs 128), a different admission point at 100 concurrent streams.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
